tasks.name: Processor: root-folder paths are checked as pack paths are
tasks.description:
Audit S21, R4 and A5 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

`Origin::File` holds a string joined by `joined` (`crates/processor/src/resolve/origin.rs`), which accepts any segment; `FilePath` (`crates/pack-types/src/file_path.rs`) refuses `\`, `:` and NUL. So `./..\..\secrets.csv` reaches `host::Files::file` as written, and a Windows host that joins it to a folder leaves the root.

## Change
`Origin::File` holds a `FilePath` (or a sibling newtype in `compmd-pack`); `Origin::join` is one call for both variants; `joined` is deleted. An import or data path that isn't a valid path gets the diagnostic an unreadable one gets today.

## Tests
Imports and data `from`s with `\`, `:` and NUL segments are refused before `Files` is asked; existing relative imports still resolve; coverage stays at 99%.

notes.text: With `Origin::File` holding a `FilePath`, the host's own document path (`Processor::new(path, …)`) must be one too. What happens when it isn't (`./a.comp.md`, `/docs/a.comp.md`, `C:\docs\a.comp.md`, an empty path)? (1) drop a leading `./` or `/` and refuse the rest with a diagnostic; (2) refuse any such path with a diagnostic and document what a path must be; (3) keep the main document's origin a plain path and check only paths documents write. → Refuse it with a diagnostic, and document what a path must be: relative, `/`-separated, inside the root.; A relative `./` naming a folder of the root (a link `[docs](./)` in another root file) joins today; `FilePath::join` refuses a folder, as in a pack. tasks.name: Every origin for a host's own documents, and the blog's share image
tasks.description:
A static site or a blog publishes its own documents, so asking its readers about each image's or data's origin protects no one, and the question gets in the way (the first post's book club opened it over the page, and the site check couldn't click a cover). Spec §15 already lets a host configure origins; this lets a host allow every origin, and the tools use it.

## Spec (§8.6, §15)
A host MAY allow every origin instead of naming them: no origin of a document's data or images is then disallowed (F028) or asked about. It fits documents the host publishes itself; a host that shows documents others write SHOULD NOT. URL schemes, a data `from`'s literal scheme and host, credentials and sandboxes' network are unchanged. Changelog entry under Unreleased; a conformance case where `allowedOrigins: "any"` loads remote data without F028.

## Code
- **Processor:** `allowedOrigins` is a list of origins or `"any"`, in the Rust API, the WebAssembly request and its TypeScript types; the conformance README says so.
- **`@compmd/sandbox`:** the image gate takes `"any"`.
- **`@compmd/vite`:** `compmd.config.json` takes `"origins"`, `"any"` or a list of `https` origins, given to the processor's request and to the sandbox.
- **`@compmd/blog`:**
  - its own origin is always allowed;
  - the build-time render shows only images from allowed origins, any other its alt text with the button, so the built page loads no image the live one would ask about;
  - a share image (`image: {url, alt}`) in `blog.config.json` for every page, a post's own in its frontmatter, written as `og:image`, its alt and a large card.
- **The website:** the blog's share image is the site's card (`og.png`), not in a post's text; `website/blog` allows every origin.
- **The first post:** the review's corrections (links, capitalisation, wording, `updated`).

## Tests
The processor and the conformance case; the gate with `any`; the Vite config; the blog's share image, own origin, and a remote image refused at build time; `cargo make site`.

notes.text: The whole card as the link: Markdown links are inline, so a link can’t hold the card’s heading and text. tasks.name: Release 0.9.0
tasks.description:
Release CompMD 0.9.0 as [releases](docs/releases.md) and `RELEASING.md` say: every npm package and the crates at one version. A minor version, since it breaks (below).

## Before the tag
- **The spec's revision:** the spec is dirty (§8.6 and §15, every origin for a host's own documents, CMD-308), so `cargo make spec-revision` cuts `1.0-draft.17`, and `SPEC_VERSION` (crate and `@compmd/processor`) and the packages' READMEs name it.
- **Release notes**, in each package's README version list:
  - Breaking: the sandbox's frame protocol is version 2 (`highlight`, `highlighted`), so a host's page and the frame documents it serves are upgraded together; the frames' policies no longer allow `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, since the host's page highlights for them (CMD-262).
  - New: the host's own code highlighter, `highlight`, in both page modes; Shiki made once for a page and all its frames (CMD-262). A host may allow every origin for its own documents (`allowedOrigins: "any"`, `origins: "any"` in `compmd.config.json`), and the blog's share image (`defaultSocialImage`, `socialImage`) (CMD-308). A document's host components are only those it uses (CMD-268).
- `cargo make ci` green on `main`, the Tauri check on Linux CI and `cargo make tauri-check` by hand on macOS.

## The release
The version in every `package.json` and the crates' `Cargo.toml` in one commit, the Tauri lockfiles after it; the tag `v0.9.0`; the release workflow stages the npm packages and waits for the crates' approval.

Every push and every publish needs the user's go; the push order is the markdown-rs fork (if it changed), then `compmd`, with `--follow-tags` for the spec's tag.

tasks.name: Browser tests that fail now and then under load: the Mermaid page in WebKit, the observer's forged report
tasks.description:
Two browser tests failed once each while 0.9.0 was released, and passed when run again on the same code. Find each one's cause and fix it, in the code if a frame is wrongly stopped, in the test if it only waits too little.

## The failures
- **The Mermaid pack's test page in WebKit on Linux** (`compmd-packs/mermaid/test/page.test.ts`, CI run 44729454247): no frame had the first diagram after 30 s, and the page had four of its six diagrams' frames, so the host's page had removed two (stopped as hung, or never loaded). It took 5 s on the run before. The test's error now prints the page's diagnostics, which say why a frame was removed.
- **The observer's forged report, O6, in Chromium** (`npm-packages/sandbox/test/observe.test.ts`), once in a local `cargo make ci`: an 8 s wait ran out; it passes alone.

## Look at
- Whether a parent stops a frame as hung, or as never loaded, when the page's thread was only busy: in WebKit a page's frames share its thread, so a long task delays the pongs and the `ready` as much as the pings (`protocol/parent-end.ts`, `startPings` and the `unloaded` timer).
- Whether 0.9.0's highlighting in the host's page (CMD-262) adds a long task where six frames load at once.
- CMD-265, the earlier Shiki load flakiness, for what was found there.

## Tests
Each failure reproduced first (`cargo make linux` for the Linux one, or the test under load), then gone over repeated runs.

tasks.name: Design: asking about remote images with less friction
tasks.description:
A revision of [remote images, asked about](docs/remote-images.md), and the spec change it needs, so a reader keeps CompMD's privacy for documents from others with less friction than a dialog that opens as soon as a page draws.

## Why
An image in a document from someone else works as a read receipt: its server learns the reader's address, the time and that the document was opened. Mail apps ask about remote images for the same reason, or load them through a proxy. CompMD asks too (spec §8.6, §15), but by a dialog the moment the first image is drawn ([decision 4](docs/remote-images.md#:~:text=The%20question%20is%20asked%20when%20the%20image%20is%20first%20drawn)), which is noise for many documents.

## What exists
- A host configures origins, or allows every origin for documents it publishes itself (`"any"`, CMD-308).
- A refused image is already inline: its alt text and a "Show images from …" button.
- A host can replace the dialog through `ask`.

## Research (light)
What mail apps do: Gmail, Apple Mail, Thunderbird, Outlook, Fastmail. Their defaults, inline prompts, per-sender "always", and image proxies (Gmail's, Apple's Mail Privacy Protection).

## Decide, with the user
- **When the reader is asked:** inline first and asked only on a click, in place of the dialog at first draw. This changes the spec's wording ("the first time a document needs an origin").
- **The inline prompt:** a bar or the image's own button; a "Show all images in this document" action; per-origin "always".
- **A reader's default:** always, ask or never, kept by the host beside the per-origin answers. Whether the spec lets a reader allow every origin at once.
- **Data and images:** they share the answers today, but a component needs its data to draw. Does data keep asking up front?
- **A host's image proxy:** the image's server sees the host, not the reader, so nothing is asked; a spec line that allows it. Likely a later task.
- Not per document in place of per origin (it weakens what an answer means), unless the examples show otherwise.

Each decision tested on example documents (a post with a remote photo, a shared notes app, a review tool, a weather post), with the gaps listed up front.

## Output
The design revised, decisions first; the spec change drafted with its changelog entry and conformance cases, for the user's go; then the implementation tasks, split as the decisions fall.

tasks.name: Sizing: the spec, its conformance cases and the processor
tasks.description:
[Sizing a component in its box](docs/sizing-components.md), *What changes*, the spec, with the processor that implements it. The spec's text needs the maintainer's go before it is pushed.

## The spec
- §9.2: `object-fit` (`contain`, `cover`, `fill`) and `object-position` (one or two of `start`, `center`, `end`, block then inline), written without a breakpoint (F009); "padding and border" (decisions 1 and 6).
- §7.4: `fit` in `mount`'s context; a component fits its box; framing is invisible to layout; natural sizes (decisions 1 to 3). §7.6: the bindings pass `compmd.fit`.
- §7, *The component's box*: a signature fence's param list as the box's defaults; F036's new meaning (decision 4).
- §5.1 and F013: the common params' names, `lang` and `dir` in a signature (decision 5).
- §12.1: the signature fence's `params`. The changelog entry under *Unreleased*.

## Conformance
The design's table: `definitions/fence-params`, `definitions/signature-types` and `resolve/params-differ-in-dash-F013` changed; the six new cases; `compmd-tree.schema.json` and `conformance/README.md`.

## The processor
The signature fence's params parsed and kept; F036 at resolving; F013 for the names; the two params validated; a signature fence's defaults under the caller's in the expanded tree, as a definition fence's are.

## Done when
`cargo make ci` is green, and the guides' chapters on the common params and on signatures say it.

tasks.name: The observer's O6 test waits for a report that may never come
tasks.description:
`npm-packages/sandbox/test/observe.test.ts`, *marks a forged report as the frame's, under its id, and acts on none of it (O6)*, failed in `cargo make ci` on 2026-11-20 (13:49), timing out at its 12 s wait, after CMD-346; it passes alone in under 5 s, in Chrome and WebKit.

## What is known
The frame's component patches `MessagePort.prototype.postMessage` when it mounts, so the forged events ride on the next `observed` report the frame sends; the test waits for them. If every report the frame sends goes out before the component's code runs, and nothing makes it send another, the forged events never arrive: a race, which a longer wait doesn't fix. Not yet proved: which report the forged events ride on when the test passes, and why none follows the patch under load.

## Do
Find the race (reproduce it under load, as `cargo make linux` or several workers at once), and fix it at its cause: the test making the frame report after the patch, or the observer, if a frame's report can be lost. No longer wait. CMD-346's way: a test that fails without the fix.

tasks.name: Design: what compmd definitions need for the no-code components
tasks.description:
The no-code components of [the first list](docs/first-components.md) stop at the same few gaps in the `compmd` definition language (spec §7.2). Each blocked task asks its own question:

- CMD-314 `link-card`: a link around the whole card; a caller's relative path in a param, linked in the pack's body, resolves against the pack (spec, *Relative paths*).
- CMD-315 `gallery`: a definition can't place each item of a slot in a box of its own.
- CMD-316 `figure`: one text as the caption and the image's alt needs the image's path as a param (the same path question).
- CMD-317 `badge`: an inline invocation has no box, and there is no inline `box`.
- CMD-348 `columns`: a definition can't test whether a slot was given.
- CMD-318 `sticky-note`: a tilt and a shadow aren't box params.

## Do
A design doc, `docs/no-code-components.md`, decisions first: for each gap, the options and a recommendation, tried on the real example documents of each component, with the conformance cases each change adds or changes. One review with the maintainer; the spec changes wait for their go, and the blocked tasks are answered from it.

tasks.description:
[What `compmd` definitions need for the no-code components](docs/no-code-components.md), decisions 1 to 6, *What changes*. The spec's text needs the maintainer's go before it is pushed.

## The spec
- §8.6, *Relative paths*: a destination that starts with a param, a field of one, or an `each` or template slot name over one resolves against the caller (decision 1).
- §7.2 and §8.1: `md.fallback` in a leaf's or inline invocation's body, F014 in a container's; interpolation in image alt text (decision 2).
- §7.2 and §12.3: an inline invocation is one inline box, styled by its fence under the caller's, a `componentInline` named `box`; layout params left out (decision 4).
- §7.2 and §8.1: `md.slots.<name>` in a definition's expressions (decision 5).
- §9.2, §9.4 and §10: `stretch-link` with W124 (decision 3); `shadow`, `rotate`, and `border`'s four logical sides in the cascade as `padding`'s (decision 6).
- The changelog under *Unreleased*.

## Conformance
The design's table: the eight new cases, and the existing ones it lists unchanged. Before the spec text, check *Gaps left*'s second point: where the processor or the host resolves a pack's relative destinations.

## Done when
`cargo make ci` is green, and the guides' chapters on definitions and the common params say it.

tasks.name: A pack's own relative links and images reach the pack's files
tasks.description:
The spec (§8.6, *Relative paths*) says a destination written in a `compmd` definition's body resolves against the definition's file, and that "making a pack's files reachable in the output is the processor's job". Nothing does it yet: the processor writes `![](./icons/star.svg)` from a pack's body into the expanded tree as written, and the host resolves it against the processed document, so it points at a file next to the document that isn't there. Found while checking [the no-code components design](docs/no-code-components.md), *Gaps left*.

## Decide first
How the expanded tree says where a pack's file is: the pack's place (`@scope/pack@1.0.0/icons/star.svg`), which a host maps to where it serves the pack's files (the Vite plugin and the bundle serve them at `packs/<place>`), or a URL the request gives the processor. Settle it with the maintainer, then the spec text, a conformance case, the processor and the hosts.

tasks.name: A diagram larger than its box scrolls at its natural size, or offers its own zoom and pan
tasks.description:
Today `fitBox` (`npm-packages/pack/src/fit.ts`) makes a drawing `width: 100%` of its box, so a Mermaid diagram wider than its column shrinks to the column's width, text and all, and `scroll` on its use does nothing: the SVG never overflows. A large flowchart or a long sequence diagram becomes unreadable.

## What the maintainer decided
- **By default, a diagram never scales below its natural size.** One larger than its box keeps that size and the box scrolls it, as `scroll` (spec §9.2) does. One that fits is placed as now.
- **A component may handle it itself instead,** with its own controls: zoom in and out, pan, back to fit. The Mermaid pack offers this as an option of its component.

## Decide first
- Whether the default is a change to `fitBox` (an option, or its behaviour for a drawing with a natural size) or to `draw()`, and whether it is the same for an explicit `width` or `height` (contain today) or only for a use with no size.
- How a use asks for the controls: a param of the Mermaid component (`controls`), or something every component can declare. Anything that reaches the spec goes through the maintainer first.

## Tests
Unit tests of the helper; the Mermaid pack's page test, in Chrome and WebKit, with a diagram wider than its column: it scrolls at its natural size, and with the option its controls zoom and pan it.

A page frame (frame mode) renders the page with no network: its images come from the host's page (`PageImages`), only those of the trees it was sent.

## Do

- `imageSources` takes the same mapping, so `PageImages` lists a pack image by the URL the frame asks for, and fetches it.
- A link to a pack's file in the frame has the same `href` as in host mode.

## Tests
The sandbox's browser tests in Chrome and WebKit: a pack's image shows in a page frame, and one not in the trees it was sent is refused.

tasks.name: An image cropped to its box: object-fit and aspect-ratio for a box's image
tasks.description:
A gallery's, a card's or a figure's images come in different shapes, so their cards are uneven. Galleries elsewhere crop each image to one shape: MUI's `ImageList` (`rowHeight`, `object-fit: cover`), react-photo-album's rows, card grids with a fixed image ratio. CompMD can't: `object-fit` and `object-position` style a component's box (spec §7.4, §9.2), and a `compmd` definition can't style the Markdown image in its body. Found in CR-45.

## Decide first
How a definition crops an image to a shape: for example, a box whose only content is an image fits that image in it, by the box's `aspect-ratio` (or `height`), `object-fit` and `object-position`, as a component fits its drawing. Write the design with the maintainer, test it on the gallery, the card and the figure, then the spec text (§9.2, §12.3), its conformance cases, the processor and the renderer.

## Tests
Conformance cases; the renderer's CSS; browser tests in Chrome and WebKit of an image cropped to a ratio, covering and contained, and printed.

tasks.name: A document's lang and dir reach its rendered page, and an example's its output
tasks.description:
Found in CMD-348 (columns): `md.lang` and `md.dir` (spec §2.1) set a document's language and direction, but the expanded tree's root (§12.3) carries neither, so no renderer can apply them: an Arabic document renders left to right unless its host sets `dir` itself, and an example (§7.8) whose own frontmatter says `lang: ar` renders in the page's direction. A component's `lang` and `dir` params work, since they are on its box.

With the maintainer: the root gets `lang` and `dir` (the document's, `dir` resolved from `lang` when not written), and a renderer sets them on the element it renders into, and on an example's output box. Then a host that renders a document into a page of its own (a blog) sets the page's `<html lang dir>` from them.

## Do
The spec (§2.1, §7.8, §12.3, the changelog), the tree schema and conformance; the processor; the renderer (the page's element, an example's box); the hosts that write a page (blog, Vite plugin); browser tests in Chrome and WebKit: an Arabic document and an Arabic example in an English page, laid out right to left. Then the columns demo's right-to-left example can use the frontmatter instead of `dir` on the columns.

tasks.name: A component's box: inline styles apply, the spec's promise, the sandbox's report and the Mermaid pack
tasks.description:
Reported by an app that runs CompMD's components in its own page: under a policy that refuses inline styles (`style-src` without `'unsafe-inline'`), the Mermaid pack's diagrams lose their styles, and since Mermaid measures while it renders, their sizes. The first commit (652fb24) gave `@compmd/pack/component`'s `draw` a CSSOM transfer for markup; a wider comparison showed that can't fix a library that writes inline styles while it measures. The design, approved in CR-64: [What a component may assume about its box](docs/component-environment.md). This task builds its "Work needed".

## Do
- **Spec** (with the maintainer's go): §7.4, the promise that inline styles apply in the box's document, kept by the processor, a frame preferred in a strict page (decisions 1, 2 and 4); §15, no CSS from a param in trusted code (decision 5), and in the note on browsers, that a sandbox's policy allows inline styles and its closed network makes that safe; `spec/CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Designs:** [running components in the sandbox](docs/running-components-in-the-sandbox.md), a trusted use in host mode needs the host's page to keep the promise, and decision 6's report; [the Mermaid pack](docs/mermaid-pack.md), it relies on the promise.
- **`@compmd/sandbox`:** report a refused inline style in a trusted component's box through the host's `error` callback, by name, from `securitypolicyviolation` (decision 6). Browser tests in Chrome and WebKit: such a component reported in a strict page, not in one that allows inline styles; both frames keep the promise under a strict host page.
- **The Mermaid pack:** revert `htmlLabels: false`; remove `test/strict-style.test.ts` and `test/strict-style/` (and the uncommitted widening of them); the README's 0.1.4 note, the pack's version and `compmd-packs/versions.json`.
- **`draw`** keeps its CSSOM transfer (decision 8).
- **The Developer's Guide**, "Your page's policy" (`guides/developers/11-the-sandbox-closer.md`): a component's drawing may need inline styles, so a strict page keeps its components in frames, or allows them knowing risks 1 and 2; a trusted component puts no CSS from a param in the page.
- **Checks:** `cargo make ci`, and `cargo make site`.

tasks.name: Every code block in a frame: language, lines, Copy, numbered; a both block folded
tasks.description:
How code blocks show on screen, chosen with the maintainer (option A3 of the mock-ups), first for `render=both` blocks, then for every code block.

## Decisions
- **Every code block in a frame:** a bar over the code names its language and its lines, with **Copy**; the code numbered (in CSS, not copied) on the host's tint, held at about twelve lines and then scrolling.
- **A `both` block folds:** its code starts hidden, the bar with **Show code** over the output. Opened, the code shows under the bar, and the output is named by a small **Output** tag in its corner, never a second bar.
- **The site's own pages too:** the spec's and the guides' code blocks (Shiki, at build time) get the same frame, from the renderer's function, so every code block on the site looks the same.
- **Buttons that work in static HTML:** the blog writes posts as static HTML, with no script unless a post has code components, so the frame's buttons are handled by one listener on the document (`followCodeFrames`), which the renderer installs and the site's page script calls.
- **No text of its own:** the bar's words (language, lines, Copy, Show code, Output) come from attributes through CSS, so a page's text and what a reader selects stay the document's.
- **The spec:** one informative line in section 7.7: a host may hide a `both` block's code until the reader asks for it; printing still shows the code, then the output. No new param.
- **In the renderer:** the base rules give the structure and the words; each host styles it (the website's CSS: the site's desk and code colours, not white).

## Tests
Unit and browser tests (Chrome, WebKit) for the frame and the listener: folded by default in a `both` block, the toggle opens and closes it, Copy copies the source, the tag shows only when open, printing shows both. The site's check for the spec's and the blog's frames.

tasks.name: Blog: the page reloads when a post is saved
tasks.description:
Today `cblo dev` and the website's dev server build the blog again for each page asked for ([decision 3](docs/blog-tool.md)), so a saved post shows only when the writer reloads the page; and the page's script, kept while the server runs (`reuseClient`, `npm-packages/blog/src/build.ts`), misses a change to the blog's components or packs until the server restarts.

## Decisions (settled with the maintainer, 2026-11-23)
1. **`cblo dev` tells the page with server-sent events.** It serves an event stream at a path of its own and adds a few lines of script to the pages it serves, never to what `cblo build` writes; an open page reloads on an event, and the browser reconnects by itself. No dependency.
2. **The site's dev server uses Vite's own full reload**: `blogInDev` (`website/vite.config.ts`) adds `website/blog/` and the files it shares with the site (`build/blog.ts`) to Vite's watcher and sends a full reload for a change there.
3. **The page's script is cached in a `ClientCache` the dev server owns**, replacing `BuildOptions.reuseClient`: the server makes one and passes it to `buildSite`; it drops the script when `compmd.config.json`, the blog's `package.json` or lock file, or a folder pack's files change. No module-level cache.
4. **Any save reloads every open page of the blog**: the list, the tags' pages and the feed change with a post's title, date or tags.

## Design first
Write these into decision 3 of `docs/blog-tool.md`, and into `website/docs/blog.md` where it says how the site's dev server serves the blog, before the code.

## Change
- `cblo dev` (`npm-packages/blog/src/serve.ts`): watches the blog's folder (posts and their files, `blog.config.json`, `theme.css`, `layout.html`, `compmd.config.json`) and sends an event to its open pages.
- The site's dev server (`blogInDev`): as decision 2.
- `ClientCache` in a file of its own, as decision 3, used by both servers.

## Tests
Unit tests for what is watched and when the script is dropped; a browser test (Chrome and WebKit) that saves a post while its page is open under `cblo dev` and sees the page change. Update the README's and the Author's Guide chapter 19's wording on reloading ("Save a post, reload its page" becomes the page following the save).

tasks.name: Spec: background takes a linear or radial gradient, with logical directions
tasks.description:
A box's `background` takes a surface token or a CSS colour (spec §9.2's table; §9.4 calls the visual tokens "a token or a CSS value", which disagree). Nothing can cut a box's corner or fade it, so the sticky note's turned-up corner (CMD-386, CR-76) leaves its yellow where the page should show through.

## Decisions (settled with the maintainer, 2026-11-23)
1. **`background` also takes a gradient:** `linear-gradient`, `radial-gradient`, `repeating-linear-gradient` and `repeating-radial-gradient`. Conic gradients are left out until a document needs one.
2. **A gradient is checked part by part, never passed through raw**, as a colour and a border are (`crates/processor/src/values/forms.rs`): its colour stops are CSS colours, its positions lengths or percentages, its direction an angle or a side. `url()`, `var()`, `image()` and any other function are refused (F009), so a gradient can't load anything or reach the page's CSS.
3. **Logical directions:** besides an angle and CSS's physical sides (`to bottom right`), a linear gradient takes `to block-start`, `to block-end`, `to inline-start`, `to inline-end` and their pairs (`to block-end inline-end`), which the renderer turns into the physical side for the text's direction, so a cut corner follows right-to-left text as a box placed with `inset-inline-end` does.

## Design first
A design document (`docs/`, decisions first, with the terms defined), reviewed before the code: the grammar accepted, written out; what is refused and why; how the logical words become physical ones in the HTML renderer (`:dir(rtl)`) and what a processor whose output has no direction does; W126 (contrast) and gradients; how a gradient prints. Tested on real examples: the sticky note's cut corner, a fade under a card's image, a striped table row. Its gaps listed up front (a radial gradient's `at` position: logical too?).

## Then
The spec (§9.2's table, §9.4), its changelog entry under *Unreleased*, and conformance cases: each gradient form accepted; a logical direction; `url()`, `var()` and a conic gradient refused with F009. The maintainer's go before the spec change is committed.

tasks.name: Processor: an edit between a component's definition and its signature fence moves the fence's params
tasks.description:
After an edit, the processor moved a resolved component whole, and only when its definition moved (`Resolved::splice`, `crates/processor/src/resolve.rs`). A host-language component's signature and box params come from its signature fence, which may be below the definition, so an edit between the two (a blank line typed before the fence) moved the fence in the tree and in validation's refused params, but not in the component. Its refused params then no longer matched, and an edited processor kept a param that a new one drops: `title=x` on `:: qr[…]` in `conformance/validate/signature-box-unknown-F008`, found by the random edits of `tests/edit.rs` once new conformance cases changed its seed.

## Fix

tasks.description:
Release CompMD 0.10.0 as [releases](docs/releases.md) and `RELEASING.md` say, then the first packs, then publish the post *The first packs* (CMD-378), which needs both: its sticky note and its badges use gradients in `background` (CMD-388), and its examples import the packs from npm. The push, with the maintainer's go: the markdown-rs fork first if it changed, then `compmd` with `--follow-tags`. The release workflow stages the npm packages for the maintainer to approve, and waits in `crates-io` for the crates.

tasks.name: Processor: the checker knows a date
tasks.description:
An app that type-checks an expression on its own (a computed field: one CEL expression worked out for every row of a table) needs the checker to say when a result is a date. Today a `date` is a `string` to the checker (spec §8.2; `crates/processor/src/cel/types.rs`, where `name("date")` is `Type::String`), so `md.today()` and `md.addDays(d, n)` check as `string`, the same as any text.

## Decided (with the maintainer, 2026-11-24)
The checker tracks a date: a string that knows it is a date, as it already tracks CSS grammars such as `length` (`Type::Grammar`). It fits wherever a string does, so no document changes meaning.

## Change
- **Spec §8.2:** a line saying the checker knows a `date`. It is a string at run time and fits wherever a string does. The `md.` functions that give a date (`md.today`, `md.addDays`, `md.startOf`, `md.dateOf`) give one, and so does a field, input or data column declared `date`. A changelog entry under Unreleased goes with it. Not breaking.
- **The checker:** `Type::declared(date)` is the date type, not `Type::String`. The `md.` signatures above return it. `join` and `fits` treat it as a grammar string: date joined with string is string, and a date fits a string. A public `Type::DATE`, or a helper, to match on.
- Conformance cases only if a diagnostic changes. None should: a date stays a string at run time.

## Tests
- `md.today()`, `md.addDays(md.today(), 1)` and a `date` input check as the date type.
- `md.today() + "x"` checks as `string`.
- A date passed where a string is taken still checks.
- Every existing case passes unchanged.

tasks.name: Processor: a public API for expressions outside a document
tasks.description:
An app wants CompMD expressions outside a document: a computed field holds one CEL expression, in CompMD's profile, worked out for every row of a table. It parses a field's expression once when it is set; type-checks it against the row's field types, refusing it with the processor's diagnostic and inferring its result type; and evaluates it once per row. A table can have 10,000 rows, so it can't build and process a document per row. `Processor::evaluate` (`processor/evaluate.rs`) works only through a whole document, and gives JSON with no type.

This takes up what CMD-84 left for later. CMD-63 made `cel` and `md` crate-private because nothing outside used them.

## Decided (with the maintainer, 2026-11-24)
- Public modules in `compmd`, `compmd::cel` and `compmd::md`. There is no separate crate, and CMD-84 stays skipped.
- A date is found by its type: CMD-398 makes the checker know one.

## Change
1. **`compmd::cel` public:**
   - `Program::parse`, `check` and `evaluate`;
   - `Scope::with` and `Values::with`;
   - `Type`, with `record`, `list`, `map` and `DATE` (CMD-398);
   - `Value`, with `string`, `list`, `from_json`, `to_json` and `Key`;
   - `Error`, with `at()` and `message()`;
   - `BUDGET`;
   - the `FunctionTypes` and `Functions` traits.

   Each gets public docs with an example. What stays internal stays `pub(crate)`.
2. **`compmd::md` public:** `Signatures`, the `FunctionTypes` for checking, and `Md::new(now, lang, tz, &dyn host::Time)`, the `Functions` for evaluating. So the `md.` functions behave in an expression on its own exactly as in a body.
3. **Values a body's frontmatter would give:** a `Value` constructor for a date (an ISO date string) and one for a timestamp from nanoseconds, so a caller builds `md.doc` as a body's frontmatter would.
4. **The diagnostic of an expression on its own:** a public way to turn a `cel::Error` into the F024 `Diagnostic`, with its line and column in the expression and its stage, as `Processor::evaluate` reports it. `Processor::evaluate` uses it too, so it is written once.
5. **Where `md.doc.<name>` is selected:** `Program::selections("md.doc")` or similar gives each `md.doc.<name>` selected by dot, with the name's range in the source in code points. The ranges come from the parse, so they skip strings, raw strings and triple-quoted strings. A comprehension variable that shadows `md` doesn't count. A caller uses it to rewrite field names, for example to store fields by an ID and show them by their current name.
6. **`Program` is `Send + Sync`,** asserted at compile time: a caller keeps parsed expressions and evaluates on worker threads. `Values` and `Value` stay `Rc`-based, for one evaluation.
7. It builds for WebAssembly, as the rest of the crate does.

## Done when
A caller can do all of this with no document, and gets the same results, errors and budget as the same expression in a body:
- parse an expression once;
- check it against a record type for `md.doc`, and get its result type;
- evaluate it against each row's values with the real `md.` functions.

An integration test does exactly that. The crate README and the Developer's Guide's Rust chapter show it. `cargo make ci` passes.

tasks.name: Blog: the watch test holds under load

tasks.name: CI: faster, failing fast, without checking less
tasks.description:
`cargo make ci` takes about 5 min 20 s from a clean build (2026-11-24), but most of the time a task spends on it goes elsewhere: reruns after flaky tests, and cheap failures found only at the end of a long run (a lint error, a JSON snapshot in another package, the guides' hosting check). Make it faster without checking less.

## Change
1. **Measure each step's time first** (fmt, clippy, coverage, doctest, docs, wasm, deny, each package's build, lint and tests, the website build, scripts), and record it here, so the rest is decided on numbers.
2. **Fail fast.** A `quick` stage at the front of `ci`: fmt, clippy, every package's lint and type-check, and `cargo check`. The slow steps (coverage, the packages' builds and tests, the website) run only after it passes. The same checks run, in another order.
3. **The website's build out of `ci`**, if what its tests need allows: `ci` builds the whole website, printing the guides' PDFs, which `cargo make site` already does and is run whenever the guides, the spec or the website change. Check first what the website's tests need, and keep whatever of it they need.
4. **An affected-only check while working.** A task (`cargo make changed`, say) that runs the packages a change touched and those that depend on them (`pnpm --filter "...[<base>]"`), and the Rust crates' tests only when a crate changed. Full `ci` still runs once before every review.
5. **Rerunning only what failed.** Say in `docs/ci.md` how to run one package's tests again after a flake, instead of all of `ci`.

The flaky tests themselves are CMD-402 and CMD-403.

## Decide with the maintainer
Point 4 changes `AGENTS.md`'s "a change is done when `cargo make ci` is green": it stays true before a review, but not after each edit.

## Done when
`ci` fails within a minute on a lint or type error, its clean-build time is measured before and after, and `docs/ci.md` says which command to run when.

tasks.name: Components the host implements: listed by the processor, mounted from `trusted`
tasks.description:
Spec §7.1: in an ambient pack, a signature fence with no component of its name declares one whose code the processor provides. A host using one, with the pack trusted in its policy and the component's mount in `createSandbox({ page: "host", trusted })`, gets its fallback: `host_components()` leaves the component out (`crates/processor/src/resolve.rs`, `host_code` returns `None` for `Body::Processor`), so the sandbox never learns it is the host's. [Decision 11 of the sandbox's design](docs/running-components-in-the-sandbox.md#:~:text=A%20component%20the%20host%20implements%20runs%20only%20in%20the%20host%27s%20page) settles how it works.

## Decided
- **The processor lists it** among the host components the document reaches: its name, its pack, its pack's trust from the policy, its `print`; no language and no code, marked as provided by the host. `@compmd/core`'s processor-implemented components stay out.
- **Only at the trusted level.** In host mode, a trusted one mounts the `trusted` mount of its name. One of an ambient pack the policy makes strict or permissive shows its fallback with `not-here`: the host's code never goes into a frame.
- **No mount, the fallback**, reported as `missing`, naming the component.

## Change
- **Spec §7.1** (and §15 if needed): a component the host implements runs only at the trusted level, in the host's page; at another level its uses show their fallbacks. Its entry under `### Unreleased` in `spec/CHANGELOG.md`, and a conformance case if the expanded tree changes.

tasks.description:
The rest of audit B25 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)), left out of CMD-301: `.github/scripts/publish-crates.sh --dry-run` packages with `--list`, so it checks the files a package holds and builds nothing, and `tauri-plugin-compmd` is published with `--no-verify`, never built from its package.

## The catch
Cargo verifies a package against dependency versions on crates.io, or packaged in the same call from the same workspace. Before a release, the new `compmd` and `compmd-host` aren't published, and `tauri-plugin-compmd` and the `markdown-rs` fork are workspaces of their own: packaging them alone fails on every version bump.

One way: package each crate with `--no-verify`, unpack the `.crate`, and build it with `[patch.crates-io]` pointing at the local crates, the plugin's in the Tauri check, where WebKitGTK is. Another: package the root workspace's crates in one call and keep the others listed.

The dry run in `cargo make linux`, on a version not yet published.

tasks.name: The Playground as a page of the website, not a package of its own
tasks.description:
Asked by the user (2026-11-25), in the review of CMD-247: the Playground is now a small page of the website around the Developer Tools, so it doesn't need to be a package of its own.

## Why

As a package, `website/playground/` (`@compmd/playground`) has:

- a second dev server, on port 5174, that the site's dev server forwards `/playground/` to, started in a second terminal;
- `scripts/assemble.ts` copying its build into the site's;
- its own `package.json`, eslint, TypeScript and Vite settings, repeating the site's;
- Vite settings that drift from where it sits: the move of CMD-247 left its dev server refusing the tools' worker (fixed in 891a7ea).

## Change

- `playground/index.html` becomes another input of the website's Vite build, beside the spec, the guides and the blog. Its Svelte page, styles, documents and examples move into the site's sources.
- The site's Vite settings take what the Playground needs: the tools' worker (`optimizeDeps.exclude` of `@compmd/devtools`, `worker.format`), CORS for the frames.
- Gone: the Playground's dev server and the proxy to it, its part in `scripts/assemble.ts`, and `@compmd/playground` from the workspace and the lockfile.
- `packs/minimermaid` stays a workspace package, built before the site.
- The Playground's tests and its benchmark run with the site's.
- The READMEs, `website/docs/design.md`, `docs/editor-support.md`, the workflows and the link check name the new place.

## Decision first: the packs' settings

`compmd.config.json` is the Vite project's, not a page's, and the two differ:

- the site: its own pack `app/`, trusted and ambient;
- the Playground: `app/` ambient but **not** trusted (readers write the documents), the `charts` example pack ambient, and `minimermaid`.

Either `@compmd/vite` takes settings by page, or one config serves both (then which trust `app/` has, and whether the landing page sees `charts`). Ask the user before writing code.

## Done when

`cargo make ci` and `cargo make site` pass; `pnpm --dir website dev` alone serves the Playground, which renders with its tools (checked in a browser).

notes.text: The site and the Playground configure their packs differently (the site: `app/` trusted and ambient; the Playground: `app/` ambient but not trusted, `charts` ambient, `minimermaid`). Should `@compmd/vite` take pack settings per page, or should one `compmd.config.json` serve both? If one, which trust does `app/` get, and may the landing page see `charts`? → Per-page settings in `@compmd/vite` (option D), designed first: the Playground keeps its own packs config (`app/` not trusted, `charts` ambient, `minimermaid`, the npm registry) and the site keeps its own. CMD-410 waits for the plugin to take them.

tasks.name: Per-page pack settings in @compmd/vite
tasks.description:
Implements [pack settings by page in `@compmd/vite`](docs/vite-per-page-config.md) (accepted in CR-137): each page of a Vite project gets the nearest `compmd.config.json`, and a project with one configuration works as before.

## Change

- **Finding a module's configuration** (decisions 1 and 9): the nearest folder holding `compmd.config.json` or a `compmd` key in `package.json`, from the module that imports `virtual:compmd` up to Vite's root; the root's, or an empty one, otherwise. The plugin's `config` option is the root's.
- **No inheritance** (decision 2); folder paths are relative to their own configuration's folder (decision 3).
- **A virtual module per configuration** (decision 4): its own `request`, `sandbox.trusted`, origins and `registry`. The root's keeps the id `\0virtual:compmd` (decision 8).
- **One page, one configuration** (decision 5): the build stops when an entry's chunks import two configurations' virtual modules, naming the modules that import each; the dev server shows the same error in the page.
- **One bundle** (decision 6): each pack's files once, compiled for the frames when any configuration doesn't trust it; one build of the frames for each distinct `libraries`; one `_headers`.
- **One registry proxy** (decision 7) for the union of the registries; a scope two configurations send to different registries stops the build.
- **`out`** (decision 10), and **watching** every configuration under the root except in `node_modules` and `out` (decision 11).
- `docs/vite.md` and the package's README point to the new design.

## Tests

As the design's *Tests* section lists them:

- Unit tests: finding a configuration, no inheritance, relative paths, conflicting registries, a page that reaches two configurations.
- Build tests: a fixture with a root and a nested configuration, including the single-configuration example's bundle unchanged.
- Browser tests in Chrome and WebKit: the trusted component in the page on one page and in a frame on the other.
- The security cases 1 to 5.

## Done when

`cargo make ci` passes.

tasks.name: @compmd/registry on the registry rules' WebAssembly build
tasks.description:
[Hosting](docs/hosting.md) H1, option (c), part 2 of 3, after CMD-19: `@compmd/registry` on `compmd-host`'s registry rules ([the registry rules](docs/registry-rules.md)) as WebAssembly.

- A WebAssembly binding of `compmd_host::registry::Resolution`, its steps and answers as JSON (decision 2). The rules do no I/O, so the binding needs no `wasm-bindgen-futures`: `resolvePacks` drives the steps itself, with `fetch`, Cache Storage and `@compmd/processor`'s `sources`, awaiting each round's steps together, and gives a pack up after its timeout (`give_up`).
- `@compmd/registry` keeps `fetch`, Cache Storage, the proxy, `fetch: "host"`'s origin check and its API; its own TypeScript for the rules goes (`resolve.ts`'s decisions, `tar.ts`, `intake.ts`, `integrity.ts`, `file-types.ts`, the metadata's reading).

## Tests

`@compmd/registry`'s tests run unchanged against the WebAssembly build. The shared fixtures (decision 7) come here, with the second runner: the cases of `compmd-host`'s `registry/resolution/tests.rs` as files in `crates/host/fixtures/registry/`, run by both.

## Open question: a host's own registry

The rules' steps (decision 2) are npm's HTTP: `FetchVersions { url, accept }`, answered with the metadata's raw body, which the crate reads. But `@compmd/registry`'s API, which its tests keep, lets a host give its own `Registry`: anything with `url`, `versions(name)` (the versions already read) and `tarball(info, maxBytes)` (`resolve.test.ts`, "may be the host's own", and the `fetch: host` test with a hand-written registry). A step that carries only a URL can't be answered by such a registry.

- **(a) Steps at the registry's level** (recommended): `Versions { registry, pack }`, answered with the versions and their max-age, or a failure; `Tarball { registry, version, max_bytes }`, answered with the bytes. Reading npm's metadata stays the crate's: a function that `NpmRegistry` (and the language server's and the Tauri plugin's registries) call on the body. Changes decision 2 and CMD-19's steps.
- **(b) Keep the steps:** the driver answers `FetchVersions` for a host's own registry by writing its versions back as npm metadata. No design change, but a JSON round trip for nothing, and the step must also say which registry and pack it is for.
- **(c) Drop the host's own `Registry`** from the API (breaking): registries only by URL, `fetch` and headers.

Also, unless decided otherwise: `give_up(pack, seconds: u64)` becomes `give_up(pack, after: Duration)`, since the tests give up after 50 ms and expect "0.05 s".

notes.text: A host’s own `Registry` (`versions(name)`, `tarball(info, maxBytes)`, kept by `@compmd/registry`’s tests) can’t answer the rules’ `FetchVersions { url }` step. Which way: (a) steps at the registry’s level, `Versions { registry, pack }` and `Tarball`, npm’s metadata read by a crate function (recommended; changes decision 2); (b) keep the steps, the driver writes a host registry’s versions back as npm metadata; (c) drop the host’s own `Registry` (breaking)? See the description. → (a): steps at the registry’s level, `Versions { registry, pack }` and `Tarball`, answered by the host’s registry; npm’s metadata read by a crate function that `NpmRegistry` and the Rust registries call. Decision 2 of the registry rules changes with it, and `give_up` takes a `Duration`.

[Hosting](docs/hosting.md) H1, option (c), part 3 of 3, after CMD-19: the Tauri plugin's `registry/` proxy for apps that process in the page ([its decision 11](docs/tauri-plugin.md)), on `compmd-host`'s registry rules.

## Tests

notes.text: The proxy fetches from registries in Rust, so the plugin needs an HTTP client: which dependency? (a) `ureq` (recommended: small, synchronous, rustls; the proxy runs on the plugin’s own thread as the scheme handler does); (b) `reqwest` (async, on Tauri’s tokio runtime, larger); (c) `tauri-plugin-http` (the app must add it too). And it reads npm’s metadata with the crate’s function, whose shape waits on CMD-422’s question. → (a): `ureq` (small, synchronous, rustls), the proxy on the plugin’s own thread. The metadata is read with the crate’s function as it is now; if CMD-422’s answer changes the steps, the proxy follows.

Q1 answered: a, the manifest gains registries, fetch and maxPackSize. Q2 is still open: pass bytes on like registryProxy, so the page hands blobs (as Vite does), or keep files in the store at packs/<place>.

Where does the plugin’s `registry/` proxy get the configuration’s registries? The bundle’s manifest has no `registries` today. (a) `@compmd/vite` writes `registries`, `fetch` and `maxPackSize` into `manifest.json` (a format addition), so the configuration stays the one source and fetching in Rust (H1) reads the same (recommended); (b) the app passes them to `init` in Rust. → a: the manifest gains registries, fetch and maxPackSize.; What does the proxy keep? I read decisions 5 and 11 as: it checks each tarball against its metadata’s integrity, reads it with the registry rules (a new public `compmd-host` function), and keeps its files in the store at `packs/<place>`, where frames load them by URL. The tarball is still passed on to the page. Right, or should it only pass bytes on? → Pass bytes on as registryProxy does; the page checks and hands blobs, as Vite does. Keeping files in the store at packs/<place> comes later, for every host at once.
Root certificates for ureq, as asked on CMD-420: allow its licence, or the platform verifier? → a, as on CMD-420: allow CDLA-Permissive-2.0 in deny.toml, for webpki-roots.

tasks.name: A pack's compmd.languages, checked, and their names in compmd/blocks
tasks.description:
The pack manifest's part of [content languages in editors](docs/content-languages.md) (decisions 2 and 3), asked for in CR-154.

- A pack declares its languages in its `package.json`: `"compmd": { "languages": [{ "id", "textmate"?, "treeSitter"?, "aliases"?, "languageId"?, "extensions"? }] }`, each grammar a file of the pack.
- `compmd-pack check` (`@compmd/pack`) checks each entry: its `id` is a language the pack's renderers `renders`, each grammar file is in the pack and parses.
- The language server's `compmd/blocks` gives each block's language's other names (`aliases`, `languageId`, `extensions`) from the pack whose renderer renders it, for an editor package to find the writer's server for it.

## First: the spec

`compmd.languages` is not in the spec or its companion, and it doesn't fit the `compmd` field as they define it:

- spec §6.4: the `compmd` field is the path of the pack's document (`"compmd": "./kit.comp.md"`), `index.comp.md` by default;
- the companion §5: an object in the `compmd` field makes the package a library pack (`"compmd": { "library": "dist/index.js" }`).

With `"compmd": { "languages": [...] }`, a pack has no way to name its document, and an object without `library` isn't specified (the processor reads it today as a pack whose document is `index.comp.md`).

**Question:**

- **(a)** The field may be an object for a pack too, `{ "document"?, "languages"? }`, a library being the object with `library`. The change goes in §6.4, the companion §1 and §5, and the changelog. (Recommended.)
- **(b)** A field of its own beside it, `compmdLanguages`, with the `compmd` field unchanged.

Which one, and may I make the spec change?

## Tests

`@compmd/pack`'s check of good and bad entries; `compmd/blocks` with a pack that declares its language's names.

notes.text: Spec change first: a or b in the description, and may I make it? → a: the compmd field may be an object for a pack too, with document and languages.

tasks.name: The language server's generate and update signature
tasks.description:
The `refactor.rewrite` actions *generate signature* and *update signature* for a host-language component ([the language server's design](docs/language-server.md#templates-code-actions-refactorings-in-1), decision 11), split from CMD-421.

## The reader

`compmd-components` reads what the source states: `compmd::analysis::Prop` gains whether a prop can be left out (`label?: string`, or a default) and its default when the code writes a literal (`{ size = 3 }`), for React and Svelte 5.

## The actions

- On a `jsx`, `tsx` or `svelte` definition fence with no signature fence: *Generate signature* inserts ```` ```compmd component=<name> signature ```` after it, from its props: each param in kebab-case (spec §7.6), its type in the short form (`number = 3`, `string?`, `a | b`), `children` and slot-typed props as `slots`. A prop whose type the code doesn't state is left for the writer as a comment, never guessed.
- With a signature fence: *Update signature* rewrites its `params` and `slots` from the props, keeping the writer's text for the params that still have a prop, dropping those that have none (unless the component takes `...rest`), adding the new ones.

## Tests

The reader's defaults and optional props in JSX, TSX and Svelte; both actions on documents with each kind of prop.

tasks.name: The language server: auto-import for a code block's language
tasks.description:
Asked by the user (2026-11-26): writing `::: mermaid` offers the import of the pack that has it, writing ` ```mermaid ` doesn't. A code block's language selects the code renderer whose signature names it ([spec §7.7](spec/compmd-spec-v1.md#:~:text=Code%20blocks%20resolve%20by%20language)), so the known packs' signatures already say which pack renders a language; no spec change.

## Design first

[The language server](docs/language-server.md): decision 7 and IN-1 cover a code block's language as well as a component's name. Settled with the user:

- **Completion of a fence's language**: after ` ``` `, the languages of the code renderers the document can name, and those of the known packs with `additionalTextEdits` adding the import to `md.import` (YAML or TOML), as IN-1 does for a component.
- **A code action on a code block** whose language no renderer the document can name renders, but a known pack does: *Import `<pack>` to render this block*. When the site couldn't load the pack, it asks to add its registry, as Q4 says.
- **No diagnostic**: a code block without a renderer is valid CompMD and shows as code.
- Two known packs rendering the same language: both offered, as for two packs giving one component name.

## Tests

Unit tests for the completion and the code action (YAML and TOML frontmatter, no frontmatter, a language already rendered, two packs, a pack whose registry the configuration lacks); the editor checks' code action list where it fits.

tasks.name: Design: a document drawn in the editor, in every editor
tasks.description:
Asked by the user (2026-11-26): what render-markdown.nvim does for Markdown in Neovim (headings, code blocks, tables, lists, checkboxes, callouts drawn in place, tables aligned as they are edited), for CompMD, in every editor as far as it allows, with CompMD's own parts drawn too (a container as a titled box, a component's params), and as little logic repeated across the editors as possible. render-markdown can't be layered on CompMD's grammars: it runs only on trees named `markdown` and `markdown_inline`.

## The direction, from the conversation

- **The language server computes what is drawn**, as intent (a level-2 heading, a container's border titled `card`, a table's column widths), not as characters or colours; each editor's package applies it with what the editor has (extmarks, overlays, decorations).
- **A plain-LSP level for every editor**: semantic tokens, inlay hints, formatting that aligns tables, code actions that edit them, folding.
- Terminal and window editors both, with a plain-character fallback where icons need a Nerd Font.

## The research, before the decisions

From each editor's own documentation, and tried where it decides something: Neovim (terminal and GUI), Emacs (terminal and GUI), Helix, VS Code, Zed. For each, what an extension or a language server can draw: replace and hide text, add text and lines, highlight, borders, images, and what each supports of semantic tokens, inlay hints, formatting and code actions. render-markdown's elements and behaviour (what it hides on the cursor's line, its settings) as the reference for the first version's scope.

## The document

`docs/editor-rendering.md`, decisions first: the server's message and its elements, the levels per editor (a table, each row from the research), table alignment as text edits or display only, the cursor line, the settings, the first version's elements, what is left out. [Editor support](docs/editor-support.md) links it. Reviewed with the user before any code; the implementation tasks follow from it.
